source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Corn (ដំណាំពោត, scientific name Zea mays) originated in Central America, specifically in the region of present-day Mexico and Guatemala, where people first domesticated it roughly 7,000 years ago.

Starting in 1543, corn was carried to various European countries by Spanish navigators. By the end of the 15th century and beginning of the 16th century, corn had spread throughout Africa and into Asian countries including China, Myanmar (Burma) and Japan; during the 17th-18th centuries the crop also reached Cambodia.

In Cambodia, corn rose to the level of a nationally classified/recognized crop by 1910. In 1936-1937, Cambodia produced corn at a considerable scale, reaching up to about 40,000 tons over an area of roughly 25,030 hectares.

Globally, corn is a staple food for humans and animals and is also used in industrial processing. In the United States and countries of South America, and in several African countries, people eat corn as a daily staple food. In Asian countries such as Japan, Korea, Thailand and China, corn is used mainly as an ingredient in animal feed rather than as a primary human staple.

Corn (Maize) is the number one most widely grown crop in the world, exceeding both wheat and rice in production volume. In the year 2000, world corn production reached as high as 500 million tons in a single year.
